body:
We have a requirement in "V52 Self-contained Tokens > V52.1 Token source and integrity"

| # | Description | Level | CWE |
| :---: | :--- | :---: | :---: |
| **52.1.3** | [ADDED] Verify that key material that is used to validate self-contained tokens is from trusted pre-configured sources for the token issuer, preventing attackers from specifying untrusted sources and keys. For JWTs and other JWS structures, headers such as 'jku', 'x5u', and 'jwk' must be validated against an allowlist of trusted sources. | 1 | |

and we have a requirement in "V51 OAuth and OIDC > V51.5 OIDC Client"

| # | Description | Level |
| :---: | :--- | :---: |
| **51.5.3** | [ADDED] Verify that the client rejects attempts by a malicious authorization server to impersonate another authorization server through authorization server metadata. The client must reject authorization server metadata if the issuer URL in the authorization server metadata does not exactly match the pre-configured issuer URL expected by client. | 1 |

If requirement V52.1.3 is satisfied, is there any reason to have additionally V51.5.3?

ping @randomstuff

comments.body: I would support keeping the requirement in v52 and removing the one in v51
I think that both are needed. 51.3.3 is about an OIDC provider trying to use the "issuer" URL (and possibly the namespace) of another OIDC provider (while still its his own keypairs).
